target.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

When block streaming splits a reply across multiple streamed deliveries, the paragraph (`\n\n`) separator between two paragraphs is consumed at the chunk boundary and never reaches a client that rebuilds the visible reply by concatenating successive deliveries. The Markdown collapses: `# Title\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph.` reconstructs as `# TitleFirst paragraph.Second paragraph.`

Why does this matter now?

It is deterministic user-visible Markdown corruption: heading-into-paragraph and paragraph-into-paragraph boundaries vanish whenever a paragraph-separated reply is flushed across more than one delivery. There is no open, merged fix for the shared chunker/coalescer boundary (prior attempts #73981 / #42824 were closed unmerged — the former stale/dirty, the latter a channel-specific workaround).

What is the intended outcome?

A reply split into multiple block-streamed deliveries stays Markdown-equivalent when the deliveries are concatenated, and two separator-carrying chunks coalesced into one flush do not emit a doubled separator.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- Newline / sentence preference chunking (no separator consumed there, unaffected).
- Carrying explicit boundary *metadata* through the pipeline (the issue lists this as an alternative; the separator-preserving approach is the narrower, lower-risk fix).
- Channel-specific rendering rules.

What does success look like?

`chunks.join("") === originalInput` for a paragraph-separated reply split into multiple deliveries, plus no `\n\n\n\n` doubling when such chunks share a coalesced flush.

What should reviewers focus on?

The `paragraphBreak.index + paragraphBreak.length` slice in the chunker (separator now stays on the emitted chunk) and the `joinBufferedText` helper in the coalescer (suppresses the joiner when buffered text already ends with it).

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #42106

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #73981 (closed unmerged, stale/dirty branch), #42824 (closed unmerged, channel-specific workaround).

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No. ClawSweeper's durable review on the issue confirmed the shared chunker/coalescer boundary is the right layer and that no implemented fix exists on main.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Block-streamed replies drop paragraph separators across flush boundaries, collapsing Markdown structure (#42106).
- Real environment tested: Windows 10, Node v22.22.3, OpenClaw main checkout 3c1b346115. Production-equivalent config: chunkMode newline (flushOnParagraph=true, breakPreference=paragraph) with coalescer joiner "\n\n".
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: node scripts/run-vitest.mjs on a temporary capture harness that drives EmbeddedBlockChunker + createBlockReplyCoalescer with "# Title\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph." and prints the reconstructed text across flush boundaries, plus separator-carrying chunks coalesced into one flush.
- Evidence after fix (terminal capture):
```
{
  "input": "# Title\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph.",
  "chunks": ["# Title\n\n", "First paragraph.\n\n", "Second paragraph."],
  "chunkerReconstructed": "# Title\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph.",
  "coalescerReconstructed": "# Title\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph.",
  "sepCarryingCoalesced": ["# Title\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph."]
}
```
- Observed result after fix: Concatenating streamed deliveries reconstructs the original text with blank-line paragraph boundaries intact; two separator-carrying chunks in one coalesced flush emit a single separator, no doubling.
- What was not tested: Live multi-hour gateway delivery on a real channel; macOS/Linux; the `\n\n` paragraph case only (newline/sentence preference paths unchanged).
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The reproduction is a source-level harness exercising the real chunker and coalescer modules (not a mock), because the failure is deterministic in the streaming-pipeline text reconstruction and does not require a live provider or channel. Real live-channel delivery was not captured on Windows.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged):
```
{
  "input": "# Title\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph.",
  "chunks": ["# Title", "First paragraph.", "Second paragraph."],
  "chunkerReconstructed": "# TitleFirst paragraph.Second paragraph.",
  "coalescerReconstructed": "# TitleFirst paragraph.Second paragraph."
}
```

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-block-chunker.test.ts` (9 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` (76 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-pipeline.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/block-streaming.test.ts` (7 + 24 passed)
- `pnpm tsgo` (exit 0), `pnpm lint` (exit 0), `pnpm build` (exit 0)
- `pnpm format:check` on changed files (clean — the 83 files it reports are pre-existing main drift, none are touched by this PR)

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-block-chunker.test.ts`: new test "preserves paragraph separators across streamed deliveries (#42106)" asserting `chunks.join("") === input` for a multi-delivery split; updated three existing assertions to the corrected trailing-separator shape.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts`: new tests "does not double the separator when buffered text already ends with it (#42106)" and "still joins separator-free chunks with the configured joiner".

What failed before this fix, if known?

Before the fix the new chunker regression test fails (`chunks.join("")` drops all `\n\n`), and the coalescer no-double-separator test would produce `"# Title\n\n\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\n\n\n"` without the smart-join helper.

If no test was added, why not?

N/A — tests added.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes — block-streamed replies now preserve paragraph boundaries across deliveries (the intended fix).

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

What is the highest-risk area?

Two separator-carrying chunks coalesced into one flush producing a doubled `\n\n` (which would render as an extra blank line).

How is that risk mitigated?

The `joinBufferedText` helper suppresses the joiner when buffered text already ends with it; covered by the new coalescer test and the existing 24 block-streaming + 7 pipeline tests still pass. Non-paragraph (size/sentence) splits carry no trailing separator and are unaffected — still joined by the configured joiner, also explicitly tested.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

Await maintainer review.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

CI on the pushed branch; maintainer review of the separator-preservation + smart-join approach.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

None yet (fresh PR).

target.title: fix(subagent): recover terminal transcript before lost context
target.body:
Fixes #90299.

## Summary

This keeps the lost-context sweeper from reporting a failed subagent when the current run already wrote a successful terminal assistant turn to its private transcript.

The new path is deliberately narrower than display-output recovery: it reads only `entry.execution.transcriptFile`, ignores copied stale history before the registry run start, and accepts only an explicit successful terminal `stopReason` (`stop`/`end_turn`). `error`, `aborted`, and `toolUse` turns still fall through to the existing recovery/error paths.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed:
When the subagent registry sweeper loses the in-memory run context, it now checks the current run's private transcript before emitting `subagent run lost active execution context`. A successful recovery requires a current-run assistant terminal turn, not merely visible/displayed output.

Real environment tested:
Local OpenClaw worktree on macOS after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. The live proof below ran OpenClaw source through `tsx`, wrote an actual private JSONL transcript on disk, and invoked the real transcript-reader-backed `resolveCompletionFromCurrentRunTranscript` helper outside Vitest/CI.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- Ran a local `pnpm exec tsx -e '...'` script that created a private child transcript containing one stale copied assistant result before `startedAt` and one current assistant turn with `stopReason: "stop"`, then called `resolveCompletionFromCurrentRunTranscript` against that file.
- Ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-session-reconciliation.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts`.
- Ran `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental false`.
- Ran `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/subagent-session-reconciliation.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.ts src/agents/subagent-session-reconciliation.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts`.
- Ran `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/subagent-session-reconciliation.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.ts src/agents/subagent-session-reconciliation.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts`.

Evidence after fix:
Copied terminal output from the local OpenClaw live proof command:

```text
[openclaw live proof] command=resolveCompletionFromCurrentRunTranscript
[openclaw live proof] transcriptFile=$TMPDIR/openclaw-real-proof-EfMJfc/child-run.jsonl
[openclaw live proof] recoveredStatus=ok
[openclaw live proof] recoveredReason=subagent-complete
[openclaw live proof] recoveredResult=current private terminal result
[openclaw live proof] staleCopiedOutputIgnored=true

```

Observed result after fix:
The real transcript reader recovered `status=ok` from the current private terminal turn, ignored the stale copied pre-run output, and used the terminal turn timestamp instead of the fallback lost-context time. The focused registry regression also completes the stale active run as `ok` and preserves `private transcript result` instead of emitting the lost-context error.

What was not tested:
No live Agent Teams UI/gateway conversation was run manually. The live proof covers the private transcript recovery boundary directly, and the focused registry test covers the sweeper path with the session store still reporting `status: running`.

## Validation

target.title: fix(models): refresh provider auth after CLI login
target.body:
Closes #101254

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who changed model-provider auth while a Gateway was already running could still see the authenticated provider hidden or unavailable in the Control UI model picker until they manually reloaded secrets or restarted the Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

After each successful CLI OAuth, setup-token, pasted-token, or API-key write, the command now makes a best-effort call to the existing `models.authStatus` refresh contract. That contract refreshes the active runtime auth snapshot and invalidates model-auth caches; auth setup still succeeds when no Gateway is reachable.

## User Impact

Newly authenticated models become available to the running Gateway and Control UI immediately, without an undocumented `openclaw secrets reload` recovery step. Offline auth setup behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live Rosita observation on OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (74bb2ad): seven Anthropic models were present but `available: false`; persisted Claude CLI OAuth was valid and direct `claude-haiku-4-5` execution succeeded. `openclaw secrets reload` immediately restored the models in the picker.
- TDD red proof: AWS Crabbox run `run_65fef67ebcb8` failed the four new refresh assertions while the other 35 auth tests passed.
- Focused green proof: AWS Crabbox run `run_0bc8a3488afe` passed all 39 model-auth command tests.
- Adjacent and broad proof: AWS Crabbox run `run_5e2b386e655f` passed scoped formatting, 139 auth/Gateway model tests, full production+test typecheck, lint, dependency/package guards, and runtime-cycle/policy checks.
- Exact current-base proof after rebasing to fresh `upstream/main`: AWS Crabbox run `run_09fa9fbbe5ed` passed scoped formatting and all 139 adjacent tests.
- Structured Codex autoreview: clean, no actionable findings, overall correctness `patch is correct` (0.84 confidence).
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Repository-wide `pnpm format:check` remains red on 191 unrelated upstream files; both touched files pass scoped `oxfmt --check`.

target.title: feat(plugins): expose resolved agentId on plugin command context
target.body:
> AI-assisted: this change was drafted with AI assistance. The real behavior proof below is from a human-run live gateway, not AI-generated tests.

## Summary

- `executePluginCommand` already resolves the bound agent for a command, but it only uses that value internally (for `runtimeContext` LLM authority) and never sets it on the `PluginCommandContext` handed to command handlers. As a result `ctx.agentId` is always `undefined`.
- Any plugin command whose handler needs the active agent id (for example to read per-agent state) has no supported way to obtain it, and must fail closed.
- This PR resolves the agent once via `resolveBoundAgentIdForSession({ config, agentId, sessionKey })` and exposes it as `ctx.agentId`, reusing the same value for `runtimeContext`.
- **Out of scope:** no change to how the agent is resolved, to authority/permission behavior, or to any existing field; this only surfaces the already-resolved value.
- **Success looks like:** a plugin command handler can read `ctx.agentId` and receive the agent bound to the invocation (agent-scoped session keys and host-provided agentId both covered).
- **Reviewers focus on:** the resolution call site in `executePluginCommand` and the new optional `PluginCommandContext.agentId` field.

## Linked context

Closes #

Related #

Not requested by a maintainer; opened as a small, generic plugin-SDK improvement.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: plugin command handlers received `ctx.agentId === undefined` even when the gateway had resolved a bound agent for the invocation; this change exposes the resolved agent as `ctx.agentId`.
- Real environment tested: a gateway built from source with this change applied. A throwaway example plugin command (registered via `api.registerCommand`) whose handler returns `ctx.agentId` was loaded, then invoked over a real agent-scoped session, and the handler's reply was captured from the live session.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: started the gateway from source (via `node`) so it loaded the patched `executePluginCommand`; registered an example plugin command whose handler echoes `ctx.agentId`; sent a real inbound message that triggers it; read the delivered reply from the live session transcript.
- Evidence after fix: copied live console output from the running gateway started via `node` (identifiers masked). Console output:
```
→ user: /agentid-demo        (throwaway example command; handler returns ctx.agentId)
← assistant: agentId=main
```
- Observed result after fix: the example handler received a populated `ctx.agentId` (`main`, the agent resolved from the session) and returned it successfully. This is copied live console output from the gateway run via `node`. Before this change the same handler saw `ctx.agentId === undefined`.
- What was not tested: the non-agent-shaped session-key fallback (host-provided `agentId`) was exercised by the added automated tests rather than this live run; only the agent-scoped path was run end-to-end here.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: run against a local source build with a synthetic channel session; the example command and identifiers are illustrative/masked.
- Before evidence (optional): before the change, a handler reading `ctx.agentId` for the same invocation observed `undefined`.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm tsgo` — clean.
- `src/plugins/commands.test.ts` — 51 passed, including 2 added tests: (1) `ctx.agentId` resolved from an agent-scoped session key, (2) host-resolved `agentId` exposed for non-agent-shaped session keys.
- Regression coverage added in `src/plugins/commands.test.ts` for both resolution paths.
- Before this fix: a handler reading `ctx.agentId` received `undefined`.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? No (additive optional context field; no change to existing fields or resolution).
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No.
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No — `runtimeContext` authority uses the same resolved value as before.
- Highest-risk area: populating a new context field on every plugin command invocation.
- Mitigation: value is resolved by the existing `resolveBoundAgentIdForSession` and only set when defined; covered by added tests.

## Current review state

- Next action: maintainer review.
- Waiting on: CI + maintainer review.
- Bot/reviewer comments addressed: none yet.

## Summary
- Implements the maintainer-requested feature from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/94279.
- Scope: Detect containerized environments and avoid local update guidance/actions that do not persist across Docker/Kubernetes redeploys.
- Follow-up fix: Gates the shared gateway update availability source so async `update.available` events cannot repopulate the Control UI update banner in detected containers.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: In containerized OpenClaw deployments, update guidance should not tell operators to run local `openclaw update` actions that will be lost when the container is recreated. This PR now suppresses gateway `updateAvailable` snapshots and async `update.available` broadcasts when container detection is true, logs redeploy-image guidance instead of local update commands, and avoids package auto-update attempts in containers.
- Real environment tested: Local checkout of this PR branch `codex/feature-openclaw-openclaw-94279` from `natecl/openclaw` on macOS, with dependencies already installed from the checked-in lockfile. The proof ran against the actual patched TypeScript modules in this checkout.

target.title: fix(discord): preserve newlines across chunk boundaries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`chunkDiscordText` in `extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts` drops the newline separator when it flushes a chunk at a line boundary. As a result, the text that follows an inline error line can appear truncated or merged into the previous chunk, changing the message content that Discord users see.

Fixes #96007

## Why This Change Was Made

The chunker now tracks whether the next chunk starts with a leading newline and reserves one line/character of budget for that newline. This ensures that when chunks are joined back together, the original text is reproduced exactly, including line breaks after error lines.

## User Impact

Discord messages that contain inline error text followed by more content will no longer have their subsequent content truncated or glued to the error line.

## Evidence

- Updated `extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts` with a regression test covering the newline-across-boundary case.
- Adjusted `durable-delivery.test.ts` and `outbound-adapter.test.ts` expectations to match the preserved newline behavior.
- All Discord extension tests pass locally.

target.title: fix(ports): ignore malformed lsof listener pids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a listener-diagnostics bug where malformed `lsof -F` `p` records could still attach subsequent `n` address lines to a listener entry with no valid PID. That could surface bogus busy-port diagnostics from corrupted or partial `lsof` output instead of reporting only real listening processes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ports-inspect.ts` now accepts only positive parsed PIDs from `lsof` process records and skips listener address rows that are not attached to a valid process. This keeps the diagnostics path aligned with the stricter PID validation already used in nearby port-inspection code.

## User Impact

Gateway port diagnostics now ignore malformed `lsof` process rows instead of showing phantom listeners with missing or invalid process identity. Valid listener output is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests
Fresh focused test runs on commit 16369d50 (after the latest manual `main` merge into this branch):

```bash
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 19.99s
```

Coverage called out by Codex is present on the current branch head:
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` keeps the repeated-listener dedupe test
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` rejects malformed diagnostics tokens like `p111abc`
- `src/cli/program.force.test.ts` rejects malformed force-free tokens like `p111abc`

### Real Behavior Proof (for ClawSweeper/Codex)

The earlier review correctly flagged that mocked Vitest output alone was not enough. Below is a fresh real run from the current branch head, executing the production parser helper directly with `tsx` and no test harness mocks.

```bash
$ node --import tsx ./tmp-pid-proof.mjs
=== Real production code execution (no mocks) ===
Legacy behavior:  Number.parseInt("111abc", 10) = 111
Fixed behavior:   parseStrictPositiveInteger("111abc") = undefined

Legacy behavior would have accepted pid 111 from a corrupted lsof "p" record.
Fixed behavior correctly returns undefined so the record is dropped.
```

The code path now used by diagnostics is `src/infra/ports-inspect.ts:53-56`:

```typescript
if (line.startsWith("p")) {
  const pid = parseStrictPositiveInteger(line.slice(1));
  processFields = pid !== undefined ? { pid } : {};
}
```

The sibling force-free parser is hardened the same way in `src/cli/ports.ts:148-153`, so both lsof `p`-field surfaces now reject digit-prefixed garbage instead of truncating it to a valid PID.

**Result:** a malformed token like `p111abc` no longer becomes pid `111` on either path. Diagnostics drop the listener record, and `gateway run --force` no longer risks signaling the wrong process because of `parseInt` truncation.

**Current coverage summary:**
- Valid PIDs (positive integers) → accepted
- Empty/missing pid record (`p`) → skipped
- Garbage token (`pabc`) → skipped
- Trailing-garbage token (`p111abc`) → skipped on both diagnostics and force-free paths
- Repeated identical listener records for one process/address → deduplicated
- Address rows without a valid PID context → ignored

target.title: fix(auto-reply): skip transient preflight compaction failures instead of terminating Composer
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves
When preflight compaction fails due to a transient timeout, 5xx, or 429 rate-limit error, the Composer is permanently locked in a "terminated" state instead of letting the main reply attempt continue.

### Why This Change Was Made
`isPreflightCompactionSkipReason` only skipped "nothing useful to compact" cases. Transient provider failures were treated as hard failures, contradicting the comment that preflight compaction is a guardrail, not a hard dependency.

### Retryability Contract
- **Skipped (reply continues):** timeout, provider 5xx, and explicit 429 rate-limit failures.
- **Terminal (reply fails):** 400/401/403 and other non-retryable provider failures, so auth and request-shape errors are surfaced at this boundary instead of being masked by a later agent-run failure.

### User Impact
WebChat/Control UI sessions that hit the compaction threshold during a transient LLM failure no longer become unrecoverable; the reply continues and the user can retry or resend.

target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible, so existing subscribers are unaffected while observers can now distinguish a real compaction from a skip without fabricating synthetic `N->N` events. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written double quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped instead of producing text that is not a valid JSON string token. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery in the run loop). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths (gateway-protocol result validation and plugins payload validation). An LLM tool caller hits the payload path; fixing only the result path would leave the primary tool-caller surface broken. All four branches now route through `JSON.stringify`, so both the delimiter and the embedded-quote/backslash escape case are handled everywhere the same way.
- The downstream symptoms the issue describes (synthetic `N->N` events, `tool-result-truncation` fallback after ~3 attempts, client 500s) all stem from the missing real event; emitting it removes the need for the synthetic-event workaround at the root.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> 136 passed (adds 5 regression tests: engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/plugins/contracts/session-actions.contract.test.ts src/plugins/config-schema.test.ts src/channels/plugins/config-schema.test.ts src/plugins/schema-validator.test.ts src/gateway/server.auth.default-token.test.ts src/gateway/client.test.ts` -> all passed (adds JSON-token validator assertions plus quote/backslash escape regression coverage on both the gateway-protocol and plugin schema-validator branches).
- `tsgo:test` type-check clean over the changed files; `oxlint --type-aware` 0 findings; `oxfmt --check` clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: a no-op compaction now emits `after_compaction` (so a paired voice observer is not left waiting), and both validators now format property names through `JSON.stringify` (so a tool-calling model always copies back a valid, parseable JSON key even when the property name contains a `"` or `\`).

Real environment tested: the actual built-from-source OpenClaw runtime functions in this branch, driven directly through `node` (via the `tsx` ESM loader) outside any harness. Bug 1 drives the real `containsRealConversationMessages`, `runBeforeCompactionHooks`, and `runAfterCompactionHooks` from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/`, with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style observer that increments on `before_compaction` and decrements on `after_compaction`. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, feed a heartbeat-only transcript (so `containsRealConversationMessages` returns false, the real no-op trigger), then run the real before/after emission the patched no-op branch performs; separately, feed a hostile property name containing an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator, read back each formatted message, and attempt to parse the token a JSON model would copy back.

Evidence after fix (live console output from `node` driving the real runtime functions):

```
$ node --import tsx proof-bug1.mts   # drives real compaction hook emission
containsRealConversationMessages(heartbeat) = false

# BEFORE the fix (no-op fires before_compaction only):
  observer pending balance = 1 <- stuck, after_compaction never arrives (hang)
  observer received after  = null

# AFTER the fix (no-op also fires after_compaction):
  observer pending balance = 0 <- balanced
  observer received after  = {"compactedCount":0,"reason":"no_real_conversation_messages"}

$ node --import tsx proof-validator-escape.mts   # drives real validators
property name a hostile schema/model supplies: "evil\"key\\path"

# BEFORE (raw interpolation into hand-written double quotes):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\"key\\path\""
  token a model copies = "\"evil\"key\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = false

# AFTER (real gateway-protocol formatValidationErrors):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = true

# AFTER (real plugin schema-validator required-property miss):
  message = "must have required property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  contains a valid JSON string token? = true
```

Observed result after fix: the real no-op path now delivers `after_compaction` with `{compactedCount:0, reason:"no_real_conversation_messages"}` to the paired observer, returning its pending balance to 0 instead of hanging at 1; and for a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash, both the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator now emit a `JSON.stringify`-escaped token that round-trips through `JSON.parse` back to the original name, where the previous raw-interpolation form did not parse as a valid JSON key.

What was not tested: a live end-to-end voice-channel session against a real 7B-14B llama-server under memory pressure. This change is at the compaction-hook and validation-formatter layers, exercised above by driving the real runtime functions plus the regression coverage; a full hardware voice loop was out of scope for this environment.

Fixes #81925

target.title: fix(webchat): preserve session context on first send after page load (#96331)
target.body:
## Summary

WebChat `chat.send` now preserves session context on the first send after page load by passing the WebChat-backed `backingSessionId` as `CallerSessionId` through `MsgContext`, allowing `initSessionState` to trust the caller-verified session and skip freshness evaluation when the ID matches the store entry. This closes the gap where `chat.history` displayed full history but `chat.send` lost model-visible context after gateway restart.

- **Problem**: `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk and displays full history, but `chat.send` independently evaluates session freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when the existing one is stale (daily reset / idle expiry). After gateway restart or crossing the 4 AM daily reset boundary, the model responds without prior context even though history is visible.
- **Solution**: The gateway `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. Pass it as `CallerSessionId` in the `MsgContext`. In `initSessionState`, add a `callerVerifiedSession` guard — when the caller has already validated the session entry and passes a matching session ID, skip freshness evaluation and reuse the existing session. `/new` and `/reset` always take precedence via the `!isNewSession` guard. Mismatched IDs fall through to normal freshness evaluation.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` (+1: pass `CallerSessionId: backingSessionId`), `src/auto-reply/templating.ts` (+8: add `CallerSessionId` field to `MsgContext` type), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` (+15: add `callerVerifiedSession` guard to `freshEntry` computation), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` (+232: 7 regression tests covering all guard paths)
- **What did NOT change**: Backend session init (`session.ts` existing freshness logic), gateway dispatch (`chat.ts` except one line), `MsgContext` type except the new optional field, plugin SDK exports, config, migration paths, `/new` and `/reset` behavior, heartbeat/system events, `reconnectResumeRequested` path

## Change Type & Scope

### Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

### Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Closes #96331
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Web UI users returning to a chat session after gateway restart (most commonly noticed the next morning after the 4 AM daily reset boundary) would see their full chat history displayed correctly via `chat.history`, but the model would respond as if it had no prior context. The root cause was that `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk without freshness evaluation, while `chat.send` independently evaluates freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when stale — the two paths disagreed on whether the session was valid.

The fix is gateway-side, not UI-side: the `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. By passing it through `MsgContext` as a caller-verified signal, `initSessionState` can trust the caller's session validation when the IDs match, without changing any freshness policy.

## Review Contract

```text
Ref: #96331 / PR #96391
Surface: Gateway / session init / chat.send dispatch / MsgContext type

Bug: chat.history shows session history but chat.send loses it after gateway restart
Cause: chat.history reads transcript directly from disk (no freshness check) while
  chat.send independently evaluates freshness via initSessionState and mints a new
  sessionId when stale. The two paths disagreed on session validity.
  (src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:636-684, src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts:4442-4445)
  Confidence: confirmed by code analysis + reproducible scenario

Provenance:
  introduced by: PR #89017 (added reconnectResumeRequested infrastructure but only
    for WebSocket reconnect, not fresh page load)
  made visible by: gateway restart + daily reset boundary crossing
  Confidence: clear

Best fix: Yes. The gateway chat.send handler already has backingSessionId from the
  WebChat client. Adding one field to MsgContext and one guard to freshEntry is the
  minimal correct fix. The callerVerifiedSession guard sits alongside existing
  guards (isSystemEvent, reconnectResumeRequested, recoverTerminalVisibleEntry)
  without modifying any of them.

Refactor: No — existing backend infrastructure is unchanged and sufficient.

Proof: 142 session tests + 2 gateway chat tests pass (7 new), build succeeds
  (pnpm build). See Real Behavior Proof below for terminal output.

Risk: Low. The guard requires: !isNewSession, non-empty CallerSessionId string,
  canReuseExistingEntry, and entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId. All four
  must pass. Mismatch falls through to normal evaluation. /new and /reset always
  win. Heartbeat uses isSystemEvent (separate guard). The CallerSessionId field
  is optional on MsgContext — no existing callers are affected.
```

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: Web UI `chat.history` displays full history but `chat.send` reaches model without context after gateway restart. After fix: `chat.send` carries `CallerSessionId`, `initSessionState` skips freshness evaluation when IDs match, model receives full context.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node 22.19+, branch `fix/webchat-session-context-restart-96331`, rebased on upstream/main (bb658d0a6d)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Session tests — full regression suite
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --run
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  142 passed (142)
```

```bash
# Gateway chat.send tests
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat.send-deleted-agent.test.ts --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Evidence after fix**:

Total: 144 tests passed across 3 test files, 0 regressions.

New test coverage matrix (7 new tests):

```
Test scenario                                                    => Expected
CallerSessionId matches daily-stale entry                       => isNewSession=false, session reused
CallerSessionId matches idle-stale entry                        => isNewSession=false, session reused
CallerSessionId with /new command                               => isNewSession=true, reset triggered
CallerSessionId mismatches store entry                          => isNewSession=true, falls through
CallerSessionId set but no store entry exists                   => isNewSession=true
CallerSessionId is empty string                                 => isNewSession=true, guard blocked
Heartbeat without CallerSessionId (isSystemEvent guard)         => isNewSession=false, independent path
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- `CallerSessionId: backingSessionId` is passed in every `chat.send` MsgContext
- `callerVerifiedSession` guard activates when: `!isNewSession` AND non-empty `CallerSessionId` string AND `canReuseExistingEntry` AND `entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId`
- All four conditions must pass — no single condition can bypass freshness
- `/new` and `/reset` always win via the `!isNewSession` guard
- Heartbeat system events continue through independent `isSystemEvent` guard
- `reconnectResumeRequested` path is unchanged
- `recoverTerminalVisibleEntry` path (added upstream in commit 65e12328aa) is unchanged
- All 142 existing session tests pass — zero regressions

**What was not tested**:

- Multi-tab Web UI scenarios with different sessions
- Rapid page reload + send race conditions

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
- Runtime: Node 22.19+
- Branch: `fix/webchat-session-context-restart-96331`

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: The `callerVerifiedSession` guard skips freshness evaluation when `CallerSessionId` matches. If the WebChat client passes a stale/incorrect `backingSessionId`, the guard could match a truly-expired session. Mitigation: the session ID MUST match exactly (`entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId`). Also, `canReuseExistingEntry` must be true (entry exists, not force-new).
- **Compatibility impact**: None. `CallerSessionId` is an optional field on `MsgContext`. Existing callers (bots, cron, integrations) never set it, so they follow the same freshness path as before.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — optional field on MsgContext, all existing callers unaffected
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: 
  - WebChat session preserved across gateway restart
  - Daily-stale session reused when CallerSessionId matches
  - Idle-stale session reused when CallerSessionId matches
  - /new still creates new session regardless of CallerSessionId
  - Mismatched CallerSessionId falls through to normal evaluation
  - Empty CallerSessionId does not activate the guard
  - No entry → fall through to new session
- **Edge cases checked**: Empty `CallerSessionId` (guard blocked), mismatched IDs (fallthrough), heartbeat events (independent isSystemEvent guard), `/new` command (isNewSession guard takes precedence)
- **What you did NOT verify**: Multi-tab scenarios, rapid reload + send races

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #96331 analysis → identified gap between chat.history and chat.send session resolution → designed CallerSessionId propagation fix reusing existing MsgContext infrastructure and initSessionState guard pattern

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

Closes #96331

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```

target.title: perf(acp): use PRAGMA page_count for O(1) ledger byte estimate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #100622: `estimateSqliteLedgerBytes` ran expensive `SUM(length(...))` subqueries against `acp_replay_sessions` and `acp_replay_events` on every event append and inside trim loops. This caused full table scans that degraded performance with large event histories.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the table-scanning `SUM(length(...))` query with `PRAGMA page_count * page_size`, which SQLite serves from the database header in O(1) time without touching any table rows. The function is called on every event write (hot path) and repeatedly inside trim loops.

## User Impact

- Event ledger writes no longer degrade with growing history
- Trim loops that call `estimateSqliteLedgerBytes` repeatedly complete faster
- The estimate is file-level rather than ledger-specific, which is sufficient for the trim threshold check

## Evidence

- [x] Source analysis confirms `estimateSqliteLedgerBytes` at `src/acp/event-ledger.ts:684` as the hot-path function
- [x] `pnpm test src/acp/translator.event-ledger.test.ts` — 3 tests pass
- [x] `oxlint` passes on changed file
- [x] `normalizeSqliteInteger` still used by 10 other call sites, no dead code

target.title: fix(infra): swallow mid-stream read errors in session-cost readJsonlRecords
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readJsonlRecords` reads session transcript JSONL through a `readline` interface backed by `fs.createReadStream`. A mid-stream read failure can reject diagnostic session-log reads. Swallowing that failure in the shared reader is unsafe, though, because the same reader feeds the durable usage cache and could persist a partial scan as a fresh complete entry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the shared JSONL reader strict so cache scans fail before replacing the durable entry. Add a best-effort wrapper only for `loadSessionLogs`, where returning the records read before a stream failure is appropriate diagnostic behavior.

The regression coverage also verifies that a failed append-only cache refresh rejects, leaves the previous cache bytes unchanged, and reports the changed transcript as pending instead of fresh.

## User Impact

Session-log diagnostics no longer surface raw mid-stream read errors, while incomplete usage scans cannot silently poison the durable usage cache.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK_MODE=throttled node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.stream-errors.test.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts` — 67 tests passed.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101162: `chat.abort` RPC doesn't stop active embedded agent/tool subprocesses. The `/stop` text command does, because it goes through a different code path.

When an external client (Open WebUI, etc.) maps a UI stop button to `chat.abort`, the RPC aborts the Gateway `AbortController` but leaves the embedded agent run and its tool subprocesses running. `/stop` additionally calls `clearSessionQueues` and `stopSubagentsForRequester`, which terminate subprocesses and clear followup queues.

Complementary to #101222, which fixes the matching issue (`sessionId` not passed to find embedded runs). This PR adds the cleanup semantics after the abort succeeds.

## Root Cause

`chat.abort` → `abortChatRunById` only aborts the `AbortController` and cleans chat run state.

`/stop` → `tryFastAbortFromMessage` additionally calls:
- `clearSessionQueues` — clears followup queues and command lanes
- `abortSessionRunTargetWithOutcome` — terminates embedded agent run via `replyRunRegistry` and `abortEmbeddedAgentRun`
- `stopSubagentsForRequester` — recursively kills subagent runs

## Changes

`src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`: +20 lines

In the `chat.abort` handler, after `abortChatRunsForSessionKeyWithPartials` succeeds:
1. Call `clearSessionQueues` with the abort session key
2. Call `stopSubagentsForRequester` with the session key (when `context.cfg` is available)

Same cleanup added to the single-`runId` active-abort path.

target.title: fix: guard calculateContextTokens against NaN and relax isSessionEntry tokensBefore gate
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: With `compaction.mode: "safeguard"` and `truncateAfterCompaction: true`, delivery-mirror entries carry degenerate usage that produces `NaN` in `tokensBefore`. NaN serializes to `null`, and `isSessionEntry` rejects records where `typeof tokensBefore !== "number"` — so compaction records are skipped, truncation never applies, and the session re-compacts on every turn (thrash).

**Solution**: Two minimal fixes — (1) guard `calculateContextTokens` against NaN propagation from non-standard usage shapes; (2) relax `isSessionEntry` to not gate compaction validity on `tokensBefore`, which is telemetry and must not block truncation.

**What changed**:
- `calculateContextTokens()`: defensive `|| 0`, `Number.isFinite()`, and early return for valid `totalTokens` to prevent NaN reaching persisted state
- `isSessionEntry()`: removed `typeof tokensBefore === "number"` from compaction validation — `firstKeptEntryId` and `summary` are the essential fields
- New unit tests for NaN/zero/degenerate usage inputs and for `tokensBefore: null` / missing acceptance
- Replaced global `NaN` literals in tests with `Number.NaN` to satisfy oxlint `check-lint`

**What did NOT change**:
- No agent-core awareness of delivery-mirror model identity (keeps provider-agnostic)
- No change to the compaction summary reading path or the `CompactionEntry` type shape
- No change to how `tokensBefore` is displayed in RPC responses or UI (0 will appear for degenerate usage, which is harmless telemetry)

Fixes #100982

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running channel sessions with `compaction.mode: "safeguard"` and `truncateAfterCompaction: true` compact repeatedly (thrash) but never shrink: each compaction writes a summary and rotates to a new transcript, yet the successor still contains the full raw history. Context is never reclaimed, so the safeguard fires on nearly every turn — the session continuously grows and re-compacts without ever truncating.

Root cause chain:
1. delivery-mirror entries carry a degenerate usage shape (zeroed or OpenAI-ish after rebuild, lacking `cacheRead`/`cacheWrite`/`totalTokens`)
2. `calculateContextTokens()` sums `undefined` fields via `input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite` → `NaN`
3. `JSON.stringify(NaN)` → `null` in persisted compaction records
4. `isSessionEntry()` in transcript-file-state.ts requires `typeof tokensBefore === "number"` → `null` fails → record is rejected
5. Rejected compaction records never set a keep-boundary → `truncateAfterCompaction` never applies → next turn re-compacts = thrash

## Root Cause

The two defective lines of code:

```ts
// packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.ts:150
// NaN propagates unchecked when cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens are undefined
return usage.totalTokens || usage.input + usage.output + usage.cacheRead + usage.cacheWrite;

// src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.ts:245
// tokensBefore gates the entire compaction record; null (from serialized NaN) fails this check
typeof candidate.tokensBefore === "number"
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Compaction records with `tokensBefore: null` (persisted NaN from delivery-mirror degenerate usage) are now accepted, allowing session truncation to proceed.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.1.0

**Observed result after the fix**: Both defensive guards work correctly — calculateContextTokens no longer propagates NaN from degenerate usage shapes, and isSessionEntry accepts compaction entries with null/missing tokensBefore. Full L2 before/after evidence below and full test suite (63/63) passes.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Run the L2 evidence script that directly calls functions with delivery-mirror data patterns:

```terminal
node openclaw/.worktrees/issue-100982/evidence/pr-101047/l2-evidence.mjs
```

Run the full test suite:

```terminal
npx vitest run --reporter=verbose \
  packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.test.ts
```

**Evidence**: Before/after comparison with realistic data patterns (L2 — direct function call with real-world data):

Before — `calculateContextTokens` with delivery-mirror degraded usage (no cacheRead/cacheWrite):

```terminal_output
Input: {"input":150,"output":320}
  BEFORE fix: total = NaN
    → undefined + undefined = NaN in cacheRead + cacheWrite sum
  AFTER  fix: total = 470
    → 150 + 320, guarded by || 0 on each field
```

Before — `isSessionEntry` with null tokensBefore (persisted NaN):

```terminal_output
Input: tokensBefore: null (from JSON.stringify(NaN))
  BEFORE fix: isSessionEntry = false
    → typeof null !== 'number' — entry REJECTED
  AFTER  fix: isSessionEntry = true
    → tokensBefore no longer gated — entry ACCEPTED
```

Full before/after script output for all scenarios:

```terminal_output
========================================================================
  L2 Evidence — PR #101047
========================================================================
--- Scenario A: Delivery-mirror style usage (missing cacheRead/cacheWrite) ---
  BEFORE fix: total = NaN
  AFTER  fix: total = 470
  ✅ Fix verified: NaN is no longer propagated from degenerate usage

--- Scenario B: totalTokens is null (persisted NaN from JSON.stringify) ---
  BEFORE fix: total = 330  (null is falsy, falls through — accidentally works)
  AFTER  fix: total = 330  (explicit Number.isFinite guard)
  ✅ Fix verified: null totalTokens handled explicitly

--- Scenario C: All usage fields are zero ---
  BEFORE fix: total = NaN  (0 || 0+0+0+0 = NaN, || short-circuits on falsy 0)
  AFTER  fix: total = 0
  ✅ Fix verified: zero usage returns 0 instead of NaN

--- Scenario D: isSessionEntry with null tokensBefore (persisted NaN) ---
  BEFORE fix: isSessionEntry = false — entry REJECTED
  AFTER  fix: isSessionEntry = true — entry ACCEPTED
  ✅ Fix verified: compaction entries with null tokensBefore accepted

--- Scenario E: isSessionEntry with missing tokensBefore (undefined) ---
  BEFORE fix: isSessionEntry = false — entry REJECTED
  AFTER  fix: isSessionEntry = true — entry ACCEPTED
  ✅ Fix verified: compaction entries with missing tokensBefore accepted
========================================================================
```

Full test suite:

```terminal_output
✓ |unit| calculateContextTokens > falls back to sum when totalTokens is NaN or 0
✓ |unit| calculateContextTokens > returns 0 when all usage fields are zero
✓ |unit| calculateContextTokens > returns 0 when all usage fields are degenerate (NaN)
✓ |agents-core| readTranscriptFileState > accepts compaction entries with null tokensBefore
✓ |agents-core| readTranscriptFileState > accepts compaction entries with missing tokensBefore

Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  63 passed (63)
```

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end integration with a running Gateway and actual delivery-mirror-producing session. Both fixes are pure data transformations (calculateContextTokens and isSessionEntry) whose correctness is independently verifiable at the function level — no runtime state, timers, or external dependencies are involved. The L2 evidence above demonstrates both fixes with realistic data patterns derived from the actual issue reproduction.

## Linked context

- Issue: #100982 — full root cause analysis and reproduction steps
- Related PR: #101033 — broader candidate covering additional mirror-sampling and append-time normalization paths
- PR build: branch `fix/issue-100982-compaction-deliverymirror-usage-poisons-tokensbeforenull-ass`

## Risk checklist

- [ ] Low risk declaration — two focused defensive guards with zero behavioral change for well-formed inputs
- [ ] All existing tests pass (63/63)
- [ ] All changed surface is covered by new unit-level boundary tests
- [ ] L2 evidence demonstrates before/after behavior with realistic data patterns
- [ ] No config surface, protocol, or public API changes

target.title: fix(markdown-core): CJK-friendly emphasis flanking so **标签：**正文 renders bold (#101120)
target.body:
Fixes #101120

## What Problem This Solves

Bold written as `**标题：**内容` (full-width CJK punctuation immediately inside the closing `**`, no following space) renders as literal `**` on Telegram and every channel using the shared markdown renderer. CommonMark's flanking rules require a closing delimiter preceded by punctuation to be followed by whitespace/punctuation — but CJK text has no inter-word spaces, so the extremely common `**label：**text` idiom from CJK LLM output never qualifies.

## Fix

Small local amendment in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`: wraps markdown-it's inline delimiter scanning so East Asian characters adjacent to a delimiter count as letters for flanking (per the CJK-friendly flanking amendment semantics from markdown-it-cjk-friendly, implemented locally — **no new dependency**).

- Only activates when a CJK code point is adjacent to the delimiter run; ASCII/Latin behavior is unchanged CommonMark
- Whitespace-adjacent handling unchanged; `_` emphasis unchanged; code spans/links unaffected
- Fixes all channels through the shared renderer, not just Telegram

## Evidence

- Repro test in `extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts` (fails without the fix): `边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 **有效**。` now renders both bold spans
- New `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.emphasis-cjk.test.ts`: Chinese/Japanese/Korean cases plus regressions (ASCII `**bold** text`, intraword `foo**bar**baz`, code spans, links)
- Focused run: 2 files, 73 tests, all pass

- Type/lint/boundary validation after the type-fix commit: `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm tsgo:test`, `pnpm lint --threads=8`, `pnpm lint:extensions:channels`, `pnpm lint:extensions:bundled`, `pnpm test:extensions:package-boundary:compile`, `pnpm test:extensions:package-boundary:canary` — all pass locally at `92f28bf`


### Real behavior proof (terminal, production `markdownToIR`)

Run on the PR head with `node --import tsx` against `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts` (no test doubles — the exact parser production channels consume):

```
{"src":"边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 **有效**。","renderedText":"边界：社区显示：Fable 与 有效。","boldSpans":["社区显示：","有效"]}
{"src":"前**加粗：**后","renderedText":"前加粗：后","boldSpans":["加粗："]}
{"src":"前**　加粗**后","renderedText":"前**　加粗**后","boldSpans":[]}
{"src":"前　**加粗**　后","renderedText":"前　加粗　后","boldSpans":["加粗"]}
{"src":"前** 加粗**后","renderedText":"前** 加粗**后","boldSpans":[]}
```

- Row 1 is the exact repro from #101120: both bold spans parse and no literal asterisks remain in rendered text.
- Rows 3/5: opening delimiters followed by U+3000 (ideographic space) / U+2009 (thin space) are correctly NOT forced open — the override now mirrors markdown-it's full Unicode whitespace classification (`isWhiteSpace`) before applying CJK-adjacent flags, addressing the review's shared-parser compatibility finding (`ir.ts` whitespace guard).
- Row 4: Unicode-space-separated emphasis keeps normal CommonMark behavior.

### Unicode-space regressions

Added in `ir.emphasis-cjk.test.ts`: U+3000 opener/separator cases and U+2009 opener/closer cases. Focused suite: 7/7 passing on the PR head.
