target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

target.title: feat(context-engine): report compaction successors as typed session targets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Context engines that own compaction report their post-compaction successor session to the host through `CompactResult.result.sessionFile` — a raw file-path string. A bare path cannot say which agent/session it belongs to or what storage mode backs it, so every consumer re-infers identity from a path, and the contract cannot describe non-file-backed sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a typed successor contract: `CompactResult.result.sessionTarget` (`{ kind: "file", agentId?, sessionId, sessionKey?, sessionFile }`) makes storage mode explicit and carries precise identity. The delegate populates it; host consumers (`adoptCompactionTranscript`, `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook`, queued-compaction rotation detection) read target-first with the raw-field fallback centralized in one helper (`resolveCompactionSuccessorTranscript`). This matches the direction main already took for runtime params in `run-session-target.ts`.

`CompactResult` is a shipped plugin-SDK surface (exported via `plugin-sdk/index.ts`, present in release tag v2026.6.11, documented in `docs/concepts/context-engine.md` for third-party engine authors), so `sessionFile` stays populated and is marked `@deprecated` naming that shipped contract, with removal planned once typed targets are the only successor contract.

## User Impact

None for existing plugins — `sessionFile` keeps working unchanged. Engine authors get a typed, documented successor contract; docs updated accordingly.

## Evidence

- Consumer map verified: all in-scope `CompactResult.sessionFile` readers migrated (`run.ts` adoption paths, `compact.queued.ts` rotation detection, delegate producer); the four look-alike readers of the runtime `EmbeddedAgentCompactResult` type confirmed out of scope at each site.
- `context-engine.test.ts` updated bridge test + 2 new tests; 206/206 tests pass across the five suites exercising compaction adoption paths.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) introduced `allowBootstrap: true` in heartbeat delivery-target resolution so plugin channel targets could be loaded on demand. However, `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause

`bootstrapAttempts` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts`:
- **Success**: key cached → subsequent ticks skip
- **Failure** (plugin not installed / config issue): key deleted → every tick re-scans

## Changes

1. **Hot path**: heartbeat call sites pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`
2. **Startup pre-activation**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` loads external plugins once before heartbeat loop
3. **Per-agent coverage**: iterates `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries (matching `resolveHeartbeatConfig` merge semantics)
4. **Session-derived `target:last`**: keeps guarded bootstrap (not pre-activatable from config)
5. **Hot reload & override preactivation**: `updateConfig` and `requestHeartbeat` (cron/manual wakes) call preactivation so externally-configured targets introduced after startup are covered
6. **Doctor caller compatibility**: `allowBootstrap` parameter threaded through `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` so doctor (which runs outside the wake loop) can resolve external plugin targets without preactivation
7. **Test coverage**: mock-backed assertions in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` verifying external-target resolution, standard-channel skip, dedup, and distinct-target branches

## Evidence

### Test proof

```
pnpm test src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts
```
125/125 tests pass across 3 test files.

### Real gateway proof

Production config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`), heartbeat `every=30s target=qqbot`, no `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` — real gateway process with qqbot/feishu channels connected.

Gateway startup:
```
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] http server listening (12 plugins…)
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] ready
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [heartbeat] started
```

Proof event timeline (appendFileSync probes, reverted from source before commit):
```
[gateway]  pre-activate: target=qqbot isExternal=false  → standard channel no-op 1ms
[heartbeat] main-plugin resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] session-route resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] TICK COMPLETE: agent=test_agent channel=qqbot to=proof-test-target totalMs=3
```

## Revision (2026-07-06)

Addressed ClawSweeper review findings:

- **P1 — reload gap**: `updateConfig()` in heartbeat runner now calls `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` before rebuilding the agent schedule
- **P1 — override gap**: `requestHeartbeat()` wake handler pre-activates requested-heartbeat override targets before the no-bootstrap resolver runs
- **P1 — doctor regression**: `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` accepts `allowBootstrap?: boolean` so the doctor path (which runs outside the wake loop without preactivation) can still resolve external plugin targets
- **Test assertions**: `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` now uses mocked `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` with real assertions (call count, `allowBootstrap: true`, standard-channel skip, dedup)
- Kept existing `target:last` guarded bootstrap unchanged

## Revision (2026-07-07)

Removed duplicate heartbeat plugin preactivation path identified by ClawSweeper review:

- **P2 — duplicate startup preactivation**: Removed `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` from `activateGatewayScheduledServices`. The `startHeartbeatRunner` constructor already calls `updateConfig(state.cfg)` which handles the initial preactivation plus all hot-reload/config-update paths. Removing the gateway-side call eliminates a repeated registry scan when an external target fails to load.
- Updated comment in `heartbeat-runner.ts` `updateConfig` to reflect it is now the single preactivation path.
- 147 related tests pass (`server-runtime-services.test.ts`, `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, `targets.test.ts`).

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency.

Related: #97638

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled:

1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace.
2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts.
3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `<location>` paths). The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides.
4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution.

## User Impact

```json5
{
  agents: { defaults: { sandbox: {
    skipSkillsSync: true,
    docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" }
  } } }
}
```

Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(auto-reply): skip transient preflight compaction failures instead of terminating Composer
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves
When preflight compaction fails due to a transient timeout, 5xx, or 429 rate-limit error, the Composer is permanently locked in a "terminated" state instead of letting the main reply attempt continue.

### Why This Change Was Made
`isPreflightCompactionSkipReason` only skipped "nothing useful to compact" cases. Transient provider failures were treated as hard failures, contradicting the comment that preflight compaction is a guardrail, not a hard dependency.

### Retryability Contract
- **Skipped (reply continues):** timeout, provider 5xx, and explicit 429 rate-limit failures.
- **Terminal (reply fails):** 400/401/403 and other non-retryable provider failures, so auth and request-shape errors are surfaced at this boundary instead of being masked by a later agent-run failure.

### User Impact
WebChat/Control UI sessions that hit the compaction threshold during a transient LLM failure no longer become unrecoverable; the reply continues and the user can retry or resend.

### Evidence
- Added regression tests and negative tests in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts` covering timeout, 429, 503, and the non-retryable 400/401/403 cases.
- Local run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts` → 54 passed.
- `oxlint` on changed files → 0 warnings, 0 errors.

### Review Follow-up
ClawSweeper requested narrowing the broad `provider_error_4xx` skip and adding negative tests; both are addressed in this update. A redacted WebChat/Control UI recording is not available from a contributor environment; maintainers can trigger Mantis proof if required.

target.title: fix(markdown-core): add CJK-friendly emphasis parsing for bold/italic
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When agent output contains `**标签：**正文` (CJK punctuation immediately inside closing `**`), Telegram renders literal `**` instead of bold. This affects all CJK users across every channel — Chinese/Japanese/Korean LLMs frequently use the `**label：**` idiom. The root cause is markdown-it v14.3.0 strict CommonMark flanking rules: a closing `**` preceded by Unicode punctuation (full-width `：`, `。`, `、`) must be followed by whitespace/punctuation to be right-flanking. CJK text has no inter-word spaces, so the common pattern `**label：**text` never qualifies. Fixes #101120. ## Root Cause / Fix **Root cause**: markdown-it's `scanDelims` classifies CJK punctuation (Unicode category P) as punctuation, setting `right_flanking=false` for `*` delimiters adjacent to them. This prevents `**` from closing when the preceding character inside the delimiter is CJK punctuation. **Fix**: Add an inline `scanDelims` override in `createMarkdownIt` that treats CJK characters (Unicode ranges for CJK ideographs, Hangul, Kana, fullwidth forms) as word characters for emphasis flanking. When either adjacent character is CJK, allow the emphasis delimiter to both open and close. No new dependency. This is a **shared/core fix** — all channels benefit because they all consume the same markdown-core IR pipeline. **Files changed**: 1 file, +47 lines (`packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`) ## Evidence ### Before/After ``` === BEFORE (pure markdown-it, no CJK fix) === "**标题：**正文" => **标题：**正文 "边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 **有效**。" => 边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 有效。 === AFTER (with inline CJK scanDelims patch) === "**标题：**正文" => 标题：正文 "边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 **有效**。" => 边界：社区显示：Fable 与 有效。 ``` ### Regression: non-CJK bold unchanged ``` ✅ **hello** world ✅ **foo** and **bar** ✅ this is **bold** text ✅ *italic* and **bold** ``` ## Change Type / Scope / Security Impact - **Type**: fix - **Scope**: `packages/markdown-core` (shared parser, affects all channels) - **Files**: 1 file, +47 lines - **Dependency**: None added — inline Unicode range checks, no new npm packages - **Security**: No security impact — the patch only changes emphasis flanking for CJK-adjacent delimiters - **Backward compatibility**: Non-CJK emphasis behavior unchanged (4/4 regression tests pass)

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated

target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS onboarding/web chat could make a slow first assistant reply look stuck or prematurely timed out when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side budget. This matters for first-run hatch/chat paths with slower models such as OpenAI 5.5, where the user expects the assistant to keep working after they describe its purpose.

The mismatch was that the macOS WebChat path needed a longer assistant-run budget and a completion observation path, while the request/ACK deadline should still fail quickly when the gateway is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short request/ACK deadline from the actual WebChat assistant run budget. The shared `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default stays request-sized so other macOS callers such as Talk Mode keep their existing timeout policy, while `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` explicitly opts WebChat/hatch into a five-minute `timeoutMs` run budget.

The shared chat UI now reads its pending/completion budget from the active transport. The default transport budget remains 120 seconds, while macOS WebChat overrides it to five minutes and waits for completion through the existing Gateway `agent.wait` surface before refreshing history. The change does not alter gateway protocol shape, auth, provider routing, model selection, session storage, schema, migrations, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant now get a realistic wait window and a production completion observation path for slow first replies instead of a premature timeout or stuck-looking state while the assistant run may still be active or recently completed.

The intended behavior is that macOS WebChat/hatch keeps gateway ACK failures prompt while giving only the WebChat assistant run, UI pending state, and completion refresh path the first-run-sized five-minute window.

## Evidence

- Current-head freshness: PR head `70ce9e068ac79a4fd092425806c45903101e06ce`.
- Current-head packaged macOS app metadata:
  ```text
  CFBundleIdentifier=ai.openclaw.mac.debug
  OpenClawGitCommit=70ce9e068a
  OpenClawBuildTimestamp=2026-07-06T19:11:13Z
  ```
- Current-head real app process and real Chat window:
  ```text
  process: dist/OpenClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenClaw --chat --attach-only
  gateway: current checkout dev gateway, port 19001, matching local gateway token
  window: id=3702 title=OpenClaw Chat bounds={Height=840, Width=500, X=710, Y=82}
  ```
- Exact packaged-app proof steps after this patch:
  ```bash
  SKIP_PNPM_INSTALL=1 SKIP_TSC=1 SKIP_UI_BUILD=1 BUILD_ARCHS="$(uname -m)" \
    ALLOW_ADHOC_SIGNING=1 SIGN_IDENTITY="-" ./scripts/package-mac-app.sh

  node openclaw.mjs --dev gateway
  dist/OpenClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenClaw --chat --attach-only
  ```
- Slow prompt sent through the real `OpenClaw Chat` input box, not through `gateway call chat.send`:
  ```text
  Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 90; echo OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.
  ```
- Visual/OCR proof from the same real packaged `OpenClaw Chat` window:
  ```text
  PROOF WebChat send, real window after UI Return key:
  OpenClaw Chat
  Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 90; echo OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.
  • Writing
  Message...
  • Gateway connected

  PROOF WebChat still pending after 35 seconds, same real window at 2026-07-06T19:55:00Z:
  OpenClaw Chat
  Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 90; echo OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.
  • Writing
  Message...
  • Gateway connected

  PROOF WebChat completion observed later, same real window at 2026-07-06T19:56:45Z:
  OpenClaw Chat
  Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 90; echo OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.
  OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE
  Message...
  • Gateway connected
  ```
- Observed result after fix: the current-head packaged macOS WebChat app stayed in the visible `Writing` pending state more than 35 seconds after a real UI send, did not show a timeout, and later displayed `OPENCLAW_UI_70CE9E0_SLOW_REPLY_DONE` with the pending indicator gone.
- What was not tested: no video recording; the proof above is terminal/visual text copied from the real packaged macOS app window plus process and app metadata.
- Regression tests and local checks:
  ```text
  swift test --filter 'OpenClawIPCTests.GatewayConnectionControlTests/`agent wait sends run id and timeout`()|OpenClawIPCTests.GatewayConnectionControlTests/`mac chat transport exposes first-run sized pending timeout`()|OpenClawIPCTests.GatewayConnectionControlTests/`mac chat transport opts into first-run sized agent timeout`()'
  ✔ Test run with 3 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.031 seconds.

  swift test --filter 'OpenClawKitTests.ChatViewModelTests/`completion wait uses transport opted in timeout`()'
  ✔ Test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed after 0.024 seconds.

  node --import tsx scripts/native-app-i18n.ts check
  native-app-i18n: entries=2752 changed=false
  ```

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Swift unit tests plus macOS terminal behavior proof.
- Target test files: `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/GatewayConnectionControlTests.swift`, `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift`.
- Scenario locked in: macOS WebChat sends `timeoutMs == 300_000`, completion waits use the transport-scoped budget, pending runs survive past 30 seconds, and pending state clears after completion.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests cover the two changed seams directly: macOS transport timeout selection and shared chat pending/completion state.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the macOS WebChat send path used one short timeout value for both request/ACK delivery and the assistant run budget, so a slow first reply could look timed out or stuck even while the gateway run was still active.
- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no regression coverage proving macOS WebChat opts into a first-run-sized assistant budget while preserving the shorter shared/default request timeout.

target.title: fix(plugins): trust official npm-only ClawHub installs
target.body:
Closes #92452

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who install the official Microsoft Teams channel through ClawHub would have the channel crash-loop when it starts, because the official ClawHub install could not pass the 6.x keyed-store trusted-plugin gate.

The reported install path is:

```bash
openclaw plugins install clawhub:@openclaw/msteams
```

On current published OpenClaw, that install records official ClawHub provenance, but `msteams` remains an untrusted global plugin. When the channel opens keyed state during startup, the runtime rejects it with:

```text
[msteams] [default] channel exited: openKeyedStore is only available for trusted plugins in this release.
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The trust predicate now recognizes official ClawHub installs whose official external catalog entry is npmSpec-only, reusing the existing official install-record/catalog matching helper instead of adding a Teams-specific bypass.

The trusted path still requires the install record to match an official ClawHub source/channel/URL and the official catalog package identity for the plugin id. Community, private, custom-URL, mismatched-package, and unrecorded global installs remain untrusted.

This intentionally does not solve broader self-hosted or arbitrary local plugin trust. Those remain separate from this narrow official ClawHub provenance fix.

## User Impact

Users can install the official Microsoft Teams channel from ClawHub and have the channel start normally instead of crash-looping at the keyed-state gate.

Official npmSpec-only ClawHub channel installs, including the same catalog shape used by Discord, can now satisfy `trustedOfficialInstall` when their install record and catalog identity match. Untrusted install sources still cannot access trusted keyed-state APIs.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Key test results

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun + success | NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun + success | Deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |
| Manual error → failure alert | NOT triggered ✅ |
| Scheduled error → failure alert | Triggered ✅ |


## Real behavior proof (Docker, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker container, `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched source at `885d605e56`.

### Latest fixes

| Issue | Problem | Fix |
|-------|---------|-----|
| P1 | Manual at-job error was disabling job (`enabled=false`, `nextRunAtMs=undefined`) | At-job error retry/disable block now guarded with `if (opts?.isManual)` |
| P2 | Manual success was clearing `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown | Cooldown clearing now inside `if (!opts?.isManual)` guard |

### Test results

| Test Suite | Result |
|------------|--------|
| Timer regression (49 tests) | ✅ All passed |
| Failure-alert (7 tests) | ✅ All passed |

### Key verified behaviors

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual at-job error | `enabled` stays true, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| Manual success | `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown preserved ✅ |
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun | Job NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun | Job deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |


## Real CLI proof (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway at `885d605e56` running with `--allow-unconfigured`.

**Terminal transcript**: `openclaw cron add` → `cron show` → `cron run` (manual, triggers error) → `cron show` (job still exists, enabled=true, nextRunAtMs preserved) → `cron list` (job present) → `cron runs` (run history with error status, nextRunAtMs unchanged).

| Step | Command | Result |
|------|---------|--------|
| Add job | `openclaw cron add --name proof-job --at ... --delete-after-run` | Created with `deleteAfterRun: true` |
| Manual run | `openclaw cron run <id>` | `{"ok": true, "enqueued": true}` |
| After run | `openclaw cron show <id>` | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |
| Job exists | `openclaw cron list` | Job still listed ✅ |
| Run history | `openclaw cron runs --id <id>` | `status: "error"`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |


## Real CLI proof at head SHA `642c3450d9` (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway built from PR head.

| Test | Command | Before (main) | After (PR head) |
|------|---------|---------------|-----------------|
| A: at-job deleteAfterRun | `cron run` → `cron show` | Job deleted/disabled | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| B: every-job manual error | `cron run` → `cron show` | `nextRunAtMs` rewritten by backoff | `nextRunAtMs` unchanged ✅ |
| A+B: counters | `cron runs` | `consecutiveErrors` mutated | Unchanged ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, or failure-alert cooldown.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker container built from PR HEAD `3d32c9baff`, Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.14.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `applyJobResult` has no manual-run discriminator — manual runs unconditionally drive `deleteAfterRun`, counter mutations, at-job disable, recurring backoff, and alert cooldown. The 12 regression tests added by this PR do not exist on main.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Build Docker image from PR HEAD
docker build --target build -t openclaw-pr83933:test .

# Test 1: Timer regression tests (includes all 12 manual-run isolation tests)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

# Test 2: Failure alert tests (adapted for manual-run isolation)
```

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`

target.title: Support compat reasoning levels for thinking xhigh
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- Allows OpenAI-compatible reasoning models to expose `xhigh` thinking when the model configuration explicitly declares API support through `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts`.
- Keeps `xhigh` hidden for reasoning models that do not declare extended compatible reasoning effort support.
- Keeps `max` conservative: it is surfaced only when compat metadata explicitly supports `max` (for example `reasoningEffortMap.max`), while plain `supportedReasoningEfforts: ["xhigh"]` surfaces only `xhigh`.

Why does this matter now?

- Some OpenAI-compatible providers support reasoning efforts beyond OpenAI's standard `minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high` set, but OpenClaw's UI/runtime capability calculation filtered those levels out before consulting explicit compat support.
- That makes valid configured models look like they cannot use `xhigh`, even when the provider explicitly lists that effort in compat metadata.

What is the intended outcome?

- Configured compatible models can advertise and use `xhigh` only when `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` explicitly includes it, and can advertise `max` only when explicit compat metadata says `max` is supported.
- Default reasoning-model behavior remains conservative for providers without explicit extended effort support.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- No new config fields.
- No change to model definitions that do not opt into extended compatible reasoning efforts.
- No local installed-runtime hotfix; this is the durable source-level change.

What does success look like?

- Existing OpenAI reasoning models keep the previous supported thinking levels.
- OpenAI-compatible models with explicit `supportedReasoningEfforts` can surface `xhigh`; `reasoningEffortMap` can map supported levels but does not by itself expose new extended levels; `max` requires explicit `max` support in compat metadata.
- OpenAI-compatible models without explicit extended effort support still do not surface `xhigh`.

What should reviewers focus on?

- The compatibility gate around extended reasoning efforts.
- Whether `max` is gated strictly enough for compatible-provider reasoning effort checks.
- Regression coverage in `src/llm/model-utils.test.ts`.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #59416
Related #74273
Related #84902

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No maintainer request from me; this is an external contributor fix for behavior observed in a real OpenClaw runtime using an OpenAI-compatible reasoning model.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: OpenAI-compatible reasoning models with explicit compat metadata for extended reasoning efforts were not allowed to expose `xhigh` thinking, and `max` needed an explicit opt-in path.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw runtime on Linux, current session using model `codex-lb-2455/gpt-5.5` with `Think: xhigh` visible in `session_status` output.

  - `session_status` output included: `OpenClaw 2026.6.1`, `Model: codex-lb-2455/gpt-5.5`, and `Think: xhigh`.
  - Targeted regression tests in `src/llm/model-utils.test.ts` pass locally.
- Observed result after fix: Compatible reasoning-level capability calculation now includes `xhigh` for explicitly opted-in compatible models, includes `max` only with explicit `max` support, and keeps non-opted-in models conservative.

Run 'blacksmith auth login' to get started.`

## Tests and validation


target.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #94224: cron jobs that intentionally produce empty replies (silent alert watchers — "watch X, say nothing unless there is something to report") fail every run with `FailoverError: CLI backend returned an empty response` even when the underlying runner returns success.

Supersedes PR #94491 which used a lane substring heuristic in the shared CLI runner. Per ClawSweeper review, the correct boundary is the cron executor.

## What Problem This Solves

Cron jobs configured as silent alert watchers fail on every scheduled run with `empty_response` errors. The `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` flag exists in the runner infrastructure but the cron executor never sets it — it is only computed for DM/group chat contexts.

## Root cause

The `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` flag is only computed for DM/group chat contexts. The cron executor never sets it, so both the CLI and embedded runner paths throw `FailoverError("empty_response")` on empty output.

## Changes

In `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts`: set `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true` on both runner calls:

1. **CLI path** (`runCliAgent` call, line 326): added flag
2. **Embedded path** (`runEmbeddedAgent` call, line 429): added flag

This is a +6 line change to a single file. No changes to the shared `cli-runner.ts` guard.

## Evidence

### 1: Bug confirmed in production binary (OpenClaw v2026.6.10)

The current npm release does **not** set `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` in the cron executor:

```
$ grep -c "allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent" \
  node_modules/openclaw/dist/server-cron-*.js
server-cron-Dcw720HP.js:0
server-cron-FMtfxqjb.js:0
```

The flag infrastructure exists in the generic agent runner but the cron executor never passes it.

### 2: Fix applied on both paths

```
$ grep -n "allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true" src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts
326:            allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true,
429:          allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true,
```

### 3: Live Gateway with active cron infrastructure

Gateway v2026.6.10 running on Windows 11, Node 24.13.0:

```
$ openclaw cron list
bdff5f85  silent-proof         every 10m  ok      isolated
72aa2ab6  silent-agent-proof   every 10m  error   isolated
```

### 4: Regression tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.silent-empty.test.ts
 ✓ passes allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent to the embedded runner  12670ms
 ✓ passes allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent to the CLI runner         697ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Embedded test uses `mockTexts: [""]` to truly exercise empty output.

```
$ npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)  Tests  26 passed (26)
```

### 5: Diff scope

```
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts | 6 ++++++
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+)
```

Shared `cli-runner.ts`: 0 lines touched.

## Verification summary

| Evidence | Type | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Production binary lacks flag | Binary grep | Bug confirmed |
| PR source has flag on both paths | Source verification | Fix applied |
| Live Gateway cron infrastructure | Runtime check | Active |
| Regression tests (embedded + CLI) | Vitest | 2/2 pass |
| CLI runner contract tests | Vitest | 26/26 pass |
| Shared cli-runner.ts untouched | Source diff | 0 lines |

**Tested on:** Windows 11, Node 24.13.0, OpenClaw Gateway 2026.6.10, pnpm 11.2.2, full repo checkout

## Why this is better than PR #94491

| PR #94491 (old) | This PR (new) |
|----------------|---------------|
| Lane substring check in shared `cli-runner.ts` | Flag set at cron executor boundary |
| Only covers CLI runner path | Covers CLI + embedded runner paths |

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```

target.title: fix(webchat): preserve session context on first send after page load (#96331)
target.body:
## Summary

WebChat `chat.send` now preserves session context on the first send after page load by passing the WebChat-backed `backingSessionId` as `CallerSessionId` through `MsgContext`, allowing `initSessionState` to trust the caller-verified session and skip freshness evaluation when the ID matches the store entry. This closes the gap where `chat.history` displayed full history but `chat.send` lost model-visible context after gateway restart.

- **Problem**: `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk and displays full history, but `chat.send` independently evaluates session freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when the existing one is stale (daily reset / idle expiry). After gateway restart or crossing the 4 AM daily reset boundary, the model responds without prior context even though history is visible.
- **Solution**: The gateway `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. Pass it as `CallerSessionId` in the `MsgContext`. In `initSessionState`, add a `callerVerifiedSession` guard — when the caller has already validated the session entry and passes a matching session ID, skip freshness evaluation and reuse the existing session. `/new` and `/reset` always take precedence via the `!isNewSession` guard. Mismatched IDs fall through to normal freshness evaluation.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` (+1: pass `CallerSessionId: backingSessionId`), `src/auto-reply/templating.ts` (+8: add `CallerSessionId` field to `MsgContext` type), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` (+15: add `callerVerifiedSession` guard to `freshEntry` computation), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` (+232: 7 regression tests covering all guard paths)
- **What did NOT change**: Backend session init (`session.ts` existing freshness logic), gateway dispatch (`chat.ts` except one line), `MsgContext` type except the new optional field, plugin SDK exports, config, migration paths, `/new` and `/reset` behavior, heartbeat/system events, `reconnectResumeRequested` path

## Change Type & Scope

### Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

### Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Closes #96331
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Web UI users returning to a chat session after gateway restart (most commonly noticed the next morning after the 4 AM daily reset boundary) would see their full chat history displayed correctly via `chat.history`, but the model would respond as if it had no prior context. The root cause was that `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk without freshness evaluation, while `chat.send` independently evaluates freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when stale — the two paths disagreed on whether the session was valid.

The fix is gateway-side, not UI-side: the `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. By passing it through `MsgContext` as a caller-verified signal, `initSessionState` can trust the caller's session validation when the IDs match, without changing any freshness policy.

## Review Contract

```text
Ref: #96331 / PR #96391
Surface: Gateway / session init / chat.send dispatch / MsgContext type

Bug: chat.history shows session history but chat.send loses it after gateway restart
Cause: chat.history reads transcript directly from disk (no freshness check) while
  chat.send independently evaluates freshness via initSessionState and mints a new
  sessionId when stale. The two paths disagreed on session validity.
  (src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:636-684, src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts:4442-4445)
  Confidence: confirmed by code analysis + reproducible scenario

Provenance:
  introduced by: PR #89017 (added reconnectResumeRequested infrastructure but only
    for WebSocket reconnect, not fresh page load)
  made visible by: gateway restart + daily reset boundary crossing
  Confidence: clear

Best fix: Yes. The gateway chat.send handler already has backingSessionId from the
  WebChat client. Adding one field to MsgContext and one guard to freshEntry is the
  minimal correct fix. The callerVerifiedSession guard sits alongside existing
  guards (isSystemEvent, reconnectResumeRequested, recoverTerminalVisibleEntry)
  without modifying any of them.

Refactor: No — existing backend infrastructure is unchanged and sufficient.

Proof: 142 session tests + 2 gateway chat tests pass (7 new), build succeeds
  (pnpm build). See Real Behavior Proof below for terminal output.

Risk: Low. The guard requires: !isNewSession, non-empty CallerSessionId string,
  canReuseExistingEntry, and entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId. All four
  must pass. Mismatch falls through to normal evaluation. /new and /reset always
  win. Heartbeat uses isSystemEvent (separate guard). The CallerSessionId field
  is optional on MsgContext — no existing callers are affected.
```

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: Web UI `chat.history` displays full history but `chat.send` reaches model without context after gateway restart. After fix: `chat.send` carries `CallerSessionId`, `initSessionState` skips freshness evaluation when IDs match, model receives full context.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node 22.19+, branch `fix/webchat-session-context-restart-96331`, rebased on upstream/main (bb658d0a6d)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Session tests — full regression suite
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --run
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  142 passed (142)
```

```bash
# Gateway chat.send tests
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat.send-deleted-agent.test.ts --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Evidence after fix**:

Total: 144 tests passed across 3 test files, 0 regressions.

New test coverage matrix (7 new tests):

```
Test scenario                                                    => Expected
CallerSessionId matches daily-stale entry                       => isNewSession=false, session reused
CallerSessionId matches idle-stale entry                        => isNewSession=false, session reused
CallerSessionId with /new command                               => isNewSession=true, reset triggered
CallerSessionId mismatches store entry                          => isNewSession=true, falls through
CallerSessionId set but no store entry exists                   => isNewSession=true
CallerSessionId is empty string                                 => isNewSession=true, guard blocked
Heartbeat without CallerSessionId (isSystemEvent guard)         => isNewSession=false, independent path
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- `CallerSessionId: backingSessionId` is passed in every `chat.send` MsgContext
- `callerVerifiedSession` guard activates when: `!isNewSession` AND non-empty `CallerSessionId` string AND `canReuseExistingEntry` AND `entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId`
- All four conditions must pass — no single condition can bypass freshness
- `/new` and `/reset` always win via the `!isNewSession` guard
- Heartbeat system events continue through independent `isSystemEvent` guard
- `reconnectResumeRequested` path is unchanged
- `recoverTerminalVisibleEntry` path (added upstream in commit 65e12328aa) is unchanged
- All 142 existing session tests pass — zero regressions

**What was not tested**:

- Multi-tab Web UI scenarios with different sessions
- Rapid page reload + send race conditions

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
- Runtime: Node 22.19+
- Branch: `fix/webchat-session-context-restart-96331`

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: The `callerVerifiedSession` guard skips freshness evaluation when `CallerSessionId` matches. If the WebChat client passes a stale/incorrect `backingSessionId`, the guard could match a truly-expired session. Mitigation: the session ID MUST match exactly (`entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId`). Also, `canReuseExistingEntry` must be true (entry exists, not force-new).
- **Compatibility impact**: None. `CallerSessionId` is an optional field on `MsgContext`. Existing callers (bots, cron, integrations) never set it, so they follow the same freshness path as before.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — optional field on MsgContext, all existing callers unaffected
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: 
  - WebChat session preserved across gateway restart
  - Daily-stale session reused when CallerSessionId matches
  - Idle-stale session reused when CallerSessionId matches
  - /new still creates new session regardless of CallerSessionId
  - Mismatched CallerSessionId falls through to normal evaluation
  - Empty CallerSessionId does not activate the guard
  - No entry → fall through to new session
- **Edge cases checked**: Empty `CallerSessionId` (guard blocked), mismatched IDs (fallthrough), heartbeat events (independent isSystemEvent guard), `/new` command (isNewSession guard takes precedence)
- **What you did NOT verify**: Multi-tab scenarios, rapid reload + send races

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #96331 analysis → identified gap between chat.history and chat.send session resolution → designed CallerSessionId propagation fix reusing existing MsgContext infrastructure and initSessionState guard pattern

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

Closes #96331
